lesson.title: Vertebral and skull development
lesson.summary: Sclerotome cells surround the notochord and neural tube, then resegment so adjacent halves contribute to each vertebra.
lesson.section: 38. Skull Divisions and Cranial Fossae; 44. Vertebral and Skull Development

steps.title: Skull Divisions and Cranial Fossae
steps.body:
The skull is divided into neurocranium and viscerocranium. The cranial fossae organize the skull base and cranial nerve exits.

Neurocranium: frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid. Viscerocranium: maxilla, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal, palatine, inferior nasal concha, vomer, mandible. Anterior cranial fossa includes cribriform foramina. Middle cranial fossa includes optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramina rotundum, ovale, and spinosum. Posterior cranial fossa includes foramen magnum, jugular foramen, hypoglossal canal, and internal acoustic meatus.

steps.title: Vertebral and Skull Development
steps.body:
Vertebrae arise mainly from sclerotome. Resegmentation lets spinal nerves exit between vertebrae. The skull develops through membranous neurocranium, chondrocranium, and viscerocranium components.

Vertebral body forms by fusion of caudal half of one sclerotome with cranial half of the next. Vertebral arch is sclerotome-derived. Annulus fibrosus is sclerotome mesenchyme. Nucleus pulposus is notochord-derived. Membranous neurocranium ossifies intramembranously. Chondrocranium ossifies endochondrally. Viscerocranium is largely pharyngeal arch/neural crest derived. Fontanelles allow molding at birth and brain growth.

steps.title: Why does resegmentation help explain intervertebral muscle and nerve relationships?
steps.body: Combining adjacent sclerotome halves places developing vertebral bodies out of register with the original somite segments. Muscles can then span joints between vertebrae, while segmental nerves emerge through intervertebral regions. The disc occupies a distinct boundary area with annular mesenchyme around notochord-associated tissue. A drawing with one somite becoming one entire vertebra misses this relationship. Follow two neighboring segments through the rearrangement and label muscle and nerve positions alongside the skeletal elements.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: Sclerotome cells surround the notochord and neural tube, then resegment so adjacent halves contribute to each vertebra. This positions intervertebral joints relative to segmental muscles and nerves. The annulus derives from surrounding sclerotomal mesenchyme, while notochordal tissue contributes to the nucleus pulposus. Cranial vault and base use different ossification patterns, and craniofacial tissues have mixed neural-crest and mesodermal origins. Avoid applying one germ-layer rule to every skull bone.
